w:r.w:t: Renewal, Reset, Sunsetting & Strategic Exit Doctrine
You will end things — or they will end you.
If you do not deliberately remove decay, complexity will strangle execution.
If you add before you subtract, you will accelerate collapse.
SCOPE — WHAT YOU ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR
of the following are true, you act
You are funding work that is not moving
Complexity keeps increasing but results do not
People defend history instead of outcomes
Everything feels urgent but nothing finishes
Resources feel scarce despite high effort
Change stalls because “it used to work”
You will use only these actions:
SCAN → FLAG → EVALUATE → DECIDE → SUNSET → EXIT → RESET → LIBERATE → REDEPLOY → RENEW → HARDEN
If you start explaining instead of executing, stop.
If it exists and consumes attention, it goes on the list.
If it is not listed, it is protected by blindness and cannot be removed.
Do not continue until the list is complete.
Go line by line through the list.
If nothing is flagged, you are lying to yourself. Go back.
What is the opportunity cost of keeping it alive?
You are not allowed to reference:
If you do, restart the evaluation.
STEP 5 — COMMUNICATE THE END (DO NOT SOFTEN)
When something is being sunset or exited:
What replaces it (or that nothing replaces it)
What happens to people, customers, and resources
No slow deaths. No indefinite wind-downs.
If anything lingers, the exit failed.
Strip controls added for past failures
If complexity does not visibly decrease, you did not reset hard enough.
If freed resources are not visible, they will be reabsorbed silently.
Drift here undoes everything you just did.
Renewal must be felt in pace and focus, not slogans.
If endings feel dramatic, you are not hardened yet.
HOW YOU KNOW THIS IS WORKING
If everything still exists, you failed.
